source.value:
The difference $Y \setminus X$ consists of all the elements that are in $Y$ but not $X.$ To represent $Y \setminus X,$ we will shade in all the area that is contained in $Y$ but not $X.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14037357/assets/5461edca3823f1cafd9f7b51528cd6eb1035e38f7f94c60177e369e2cdd5f350.png)

Therefore, the difference is

$$
Y \setminus X = \{ 4 \}.
$$

source.value: Given the sets $X = \{ 2, 5, 7, 8 \},$ $Y = \{ 1, 3, 5 \},$ and $Z = \{ 2, 4, 6, 8 \},$ find $X \setminus Y,$ $Y \setminus Z,$ and $Z \setminus X.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-7159

source.question: e-7159
source.value:
The set $X \setminus Y$ is the set of all elements belonging to $X$ but *not* $Y.$ Note that the element $5 \in Y$ is also in $X,$ so we must remove it. Hence, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}X∖Y & =X-Y \\  & ={2,5,7,8}-{1,3,5} \\  & ={2,7,8}.\end{aligned}
$$

The set $Y \setminus Z$ is the set of all elements belonging to $Y$ but *not* $Z.$ Note that none of the elements of $Y$ are in $Z.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Y∖Z & =Y-Z \\  & ={1,3,5}-{2,4,6,8} \\  & ={1,3,5}.\end{aligned}
$$

The set $Z \setminus X$ is the set of all elements belonging to $Z$ but *not* $X.$ Note that the elements $2,8 \in Z$ are also in $X,$ so we must remove them. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Z∖X & =Z-X \\  & ={2,4,6,8}-{2,5,7,8} \\  & ={4,6}.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value: Let $A$ be the set of all multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ and let $B$ be the set of all multiples of $6$ that are greater than $0.$ What is $A \setminus B?$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-7160

source.question: e-7160
source.value:
The multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A = \{ 4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32, 36 \ldots \}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $6$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B = \{ 6,12,18,24,30,36,\ldots \}.
$$

Now, $A \setminus B$ is the *difference* of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $A$ but *not* in $B.$

The elements of $A$ that are also in $B$ are $12, 24, 36$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $A.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∖B & =A-B \\  & ={4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,…}-{6,12,18,24,30,36,…} \\  & ={4,8,16,20,28,32,…}.\end{aligned}
$$
